independent_review.text:
# Independent review: eight menu source decisions

Scope is main at 4c29be143432bcb5b2ca99d4f83ca6ff162b4554. V3 patch SHA-256 77801434785644ab0ff382f33dde8800e6d0efb4e3208ab9791f73439e940b2b, manifest SHA-256 54cd7ebd1ef23d5fecea66dda6c6f6d5630523880237659e8cc1ae93783452bf. Strict whitespace application to a private index passed, producing tree 06af87af40455a2d22ee50968c4cde7f00ddb4a1; all ten afterimages match the frozen candidate bytes. The 1,697-row ledger has exactly the eight selected rows changed, same order; bytes outside those exact eight JSON nodes are identical and the complete prior entries are retained in the reviewed evidence. V2→V3 changes only the 4b report and corresponding row wording, preserving the other seven reports and historical snapshot.

All eight raw upstream commits match retained census object bytes and SHA-256, and their complete changed path sets match Git diff-tree and census. Their embedded full patches match Git bytes. All 12 retained Material16 sources match the actual tagged Git blobs and hashes, all 28 current product source members match the 4c29 commit, and all five referenced peer files match installed Material22.1.7 bytes. No peer dependency closure or runtime is newly qualified.

* 05d changes the modern menu divider token property. Historical/owned legacy menu styling has no corresponding menu-scoped modern token; separately owned divider theming remains, and color in every theme is not established.
* 355 adds `:has(.mat-mdc-menu-content:empty) { display:none }` during modern ng-animation. The owned SCSS retains tagged16 pointer suppression without empty hiding; its hash matches the earlier b5df repaired SCSS. I rehashed the prior native Chromium149 173/176 bdc baseline and 176/176 b5df candidate reports and their tarballs. Those historical results used their own artifact and earlier test source, not 4c29; tagged16 browser execution was not performed. The source decision does not require consumer CSS and does not claim all motion/browser behavior.
* 367 changes context-menu-trigger backdrop opt-in. Legacy has no exported modern context trigger; its distinct root/submenu hasBackdrop default logic is retained. No modern feature equivalence is asserted.
* 4b removes current peer factory/provider exports/module wiring and inlines current defaults. Tagged16 legacy module used the peer scroll-strategy provider and exposed the legacy scroll token; tagged16 legacy public API did not export legacy-named factory/provider aliases. The addon owns its Overlay-based factory/provider, retains module wiring, and additionally exports those addon aliases. Its legacy default-options token is the public peer token, not the removed default-options factory. V3 correctly distinguishes these facts.
* 4d removes explicit OnPush metadata from modern menu/menu-item and two test hosts. Legacy retains its historical OnPush metadata and owned notification code; no claim of equal peer default scheduling is made.
* 9d adds modern readable panelClass and initializes its backing string. Tagged16 and owned legacy panelClass are setter-only; reading it, including through the classList getter, yields undefined rather than the modern getter result. This is an explicit reachable contract difference, not a claim of an inherited fix.
* b151 prevents lazy content detachment by a trigger after ownership transfers. Owned WeakMap ownership, generation checks and the reentrant guard after overlay detach protect the corresponding scope through local code; that does not prove every possible reentrant sequence.
* c928 adds a modern triggerIconName harness filter, icon dependency and tests. The legacy harness retains its finite historical triggerText filter and does not provide the later modern icon option. This is not peer-harness delegation.

The identity checker cannot establish the truth or relevance of a source judgment merely because all cited files hash correctly; manual hunk review is required. The direct helper controls are not by themselves production-dispatch proof. I ran the unchanged production CLI using an existing detached worktree at exact 4c29 and the frozen candidate evidence. The union of insufficient/evidence SHA IDs decreased 834→826 by exactly the eight target SHAs with no additions; independently changing a current source, each embedded full diff, and the branch binding reopened all eight in each run. All five overall CLI invocations exited nonzero because unrelated aggregate obligations remain. Retained producer state is production-state.json, and baseline/candidate/mutant full JSON reports are alongside this review. The linked node_modules dependency closure was not independently frozen. No current packed, browser, accessibility, G11, security or release qualification follows. Later canonical HEAD requires explicit reconciliation.

limitations: Source-only decisions; historical browser observations retain original subjects.
No new current browser, whole checker, security, G11, release or 21.x qualification.
Menu public export extras remain a separate open contract review.
